newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: International stock pickers lift NZ index by close.
newsitem.headline: International stock pickers lift NZ index by close.

text.p: * Selective interest in handful of stocks lifts quiet market
* Telecom dominates with another rise and half mkt volume
* Fletcher Building plays catch-up after sellers back off
Price movements by close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +7.29 at 2,407.50

738 +4 * Other movers- +10 +6

New Zealand's share market took another boost from selective offshore buying interest on Thursday as a handful of blue-chips dominated an otherwise sideways session and lifted the main indices by the close.
The NZ top 40 index closed up 7.29 points at 2,407.50 with total volume of NZ$72.6 million in value, of which Telecom alone accounted for about $30 million.

Brokers said the week's theme continued to be solid international demand for Telecom, up four cents at $7.38, and Fletcher Forest, up six at $2.10, reaping the continued rewards of buying interest in its cyclical sector.

JB Were's Luke Koekoek said Fletcher Forest was partly running up to match some of the gains seen in recent weeks by Carter Holt Harvey and Fletcher Paper FLTCP.NZ amid renewed confidence in the prospects for forest products.
"It's beginning to rub off on Fletcher Forest, and hence it hit $2.10 today on active trade, but it's not the locals that are pushing the stock up to these levels, it's the overseas guys," he said.
While Forest's business is in a slightly different segment to the pure paper or products stocks, it is seen as a more defensive play in the commodity cycle, brokers added.
Dealers noted that other blue chips like Lion Nathan, Air New Zealand and Brierley Investments again stood still in a broadly directionless market.
One noteable mover was Fletcher Building, jumping a sharp 10 cents to $4.32, after some sizeable selling that had been overhanging the market appeared to move away, they added.
Koekoek said there was some renewed interest in the building materials and related sectors such as steel, where a handful of stocks could be seen as an economic recovery play.
"There are not that many (shares) out there for a pure New Zealand economy play other than Telecom. Fletcher Building fits in the category well," he said.

With the country's other financial markets all on hold awaiting next week's budget and monetary policy statement, dealers said they saw little prospect of any sudden new impulse eiher way in the market as the week draws to a close.
